title: Routing & fallback brief — internal announcement scratch
body:
Quick scratchpad for a short company-facing announcement + Q&A for the lightweight update next week. Not polished — just notes and suggested phrasing.

High level goal:
- Explain a small change to default routing + fallback policy we plan to flip on Friday (beta). Focus: reduce failed requests during regional capacity spikes, keep latency SLO where possible.

One-line announcement (for #general):
- TL;DR: We9re enabling a new routing fallback that will automatically route requests to compatible model variants when regional capacity is constrained — should reduce 5xxs and keep most apps online. Rolling this Friday, opt-out available.

Talking points for 2-min all-hands mention:
- Why: occasional regional outages and sudden demand bursts are causing errors for some hosted customers; engineered fallback reduces customer-visible failures without human ops.
- What: requests will try primary region -> if capacity unavailable will route to a compatible variant in nearby region or lower-cost instance tier (same model family, quantized where applicable).
- Impact: expected reduction in 5xxs by ~60% for identified flows; median latency change ~+40ms in fallback cases; rate limiting and data residency fallbacks honored.
- Controls: orgs on Dedicated can pin regions and opt out; Private installs unaffected. Console rollout includes toggle and audit logs.

Anticipated questions + short answers (for Slack thread/FAQ):
Q: Will customer data leave region?
A: No — routing respects data residency policies. If a tenant has "regional-only" enabled, we won9t route outside region; for others, we route to nearest compatible region.

Q: Will model outputs differ?
A: Slight variation is possible if routing to a quantized variant. We9re only routing to verified-compatible variants and have eval thresholds; quality regressions are monitored and can auto-roll back.

Q: How to opt out?
A: Console -> Model routing -> toggle off for org. CLI: redwood routing set --org <org> --mode strict. Support can file RED-XXXX to request org-wide exclusion.

Q: Who to contact if we see regression?
A: Ping #serving-runtime and @oncall-sre; escalate to Marco (cc in email) if rollback needed.

Notes for the message tone: keep concise, emphasize reliability and that this is reversible and opt-out. Avoid technical kernel details in public message.

Slack post draft (two variants):
- Short: "Rolling a routing fallback Friday to reduce customer-visible failures during regional spikes. System will only route to verified-compatible model variants; Dedicated customers can opt out. Details + FAQ: <link>."
- Longer (for pinned thread): include the Why/What/Impact + quick opt-out steps + link to the console toggle + contact.

Open questions / decisions needed (to resolve before announcement):
- Confirm rollback SLA window and contact list (Leah to confirm ops on-call rota for Friday 09:00-18:00 PDT).
- Finalize console toggle copy — product review needed (Sonia).
- Confirm metric dashboard link to include in message (Marco to share panel id).

Action items (owner):
- Leah: confirm on-call coverage and prepare runbook snippet (due 2025-06-11).
- Sonia: review and finalize console copy + opt-out CLI help text (due 2025-06-11).
- Marco: share dashboard panels and expected graph images for the thread (due 2025-06-11).
- Ryan (me): finalize Slack announcement + thread and send for quick review by EOD 2025-06-12.

Draft email subject lines (short experimentation):
- "Planned routing fallback to reduce regional errors — opt-out available"
- "Reducing customer-visible failures: routing fallback rolling Friday"

Rough links to paste in announcement thread:
- Console toggle (placeholder): https://console.redwood.ai/models/routing
- Dashboard (waiting on Marco): placeholder panel https://grafana.redwood.local/d/abcd/routing-fallback

Scratch notes (internal talking points for follow-ups):
- Be ready to call out "verified-compatible" definition: same architecture family, same tokenization, eval delta < 2% on key test set.
- We have fallback telemetry to drive automatic rollback if error rate spikes beyond threshold for >5m.
- Keep messaging non-technical for product teams; include a technical appendix link for engs.

-- end scratch — keep concise, send around for review.
